_readme: MONEY-1379 — a GCP-integration GAUGE (or count), grouped, compared to a ceiling.
`max` over the window for gauges: a gauge that TOUCHED the ceiling once in
the window is the question, not its average. `sum` + `.as_count()` for the
scheduler-errors count (agg/suffix placeholders). Scope is always a NAMED
subscription, service or job pattern — never {*} — because the same project
carries local pull subscriptions that are never drained and two algo-*
TIME and SPACE aggregation are SEPARATE placeholders, and collapsing them
into one was a real defect (MONEY-1379 review). Datadog's monitor grammar is `time_aggr(window):space_aggr:metric{...}` — the LEADING aggregator
aggregates over the WINDOW and the inner one ACROSS SERIES. They are
rarely the same answer: `gcp.run.container.instance_count` carries a `state`
tag (active / idle), so `max:` over it reads max(active, idle) rather than
the instance count — a service sitting at its cap of 20 as 12 active + 8
idle evaluates to 12 and never crosses a `> 18` critical. It can only ever
UNDER-report, so the failure mode is a silent miss. Counts and totals space-
aggregate with `sum`; an AGE (oldest_unacked) genuinely wants `max`, because
the oldest message is the question.
_query_brace_rationale: `{{{scope}}}` and `{{{group}}}` are THREE braces on purpose, and they are not
a typo for a Datadog template variable.
Datadog's query language writes a scope and a group-by inside LITERAL braces:
dd_render's fill() matches `/\{\{(\w+)\}\}/g`, so of the three braces it
consumes the inner two as the placeholder `{{scope}}` and leaves the outer
one as query syntax. Rendered, `scope="subscription_id:*-prod-push"` gives
This means the VARIABLE VALUE must NOT carry its own braces. Passing
is both invalid query syntax and, worse, looks like a Datadog template
name: [{{env}}] {{label}}
